questions.question: Who among the following was greatest ruler of Pratihara Dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mihir Bhoja​.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mihir Bhoja** was the greatest ruler of the** Pratihara Dynasty.**
 
• The Pratiharas or the Gurjar Pratiharas **rose to power after the fall of the Pushyabuti Dynasty.**
 
• There are major two lineages of Pratihara known that was** founded by Harichandra and Nagabhatta.**
 
• The line of** Harichandra (6th -9th century AD) ruled over Marwar** in Rajasthan and that of **Nagabhatta I (8th - 11th century AD) ruled over Ujjain and Kannauj.**
 
• Bhoja or** Mihir Bhoja was the greatest ruler **of this dynasty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Was succeeded by Mihir Bhoja.

questions.question: Who was the President of India during the State of Emergency (1975-77)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2.** Dr. Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed was the President of India during the State of Emergency (1975-77).

 
• It was declared during the time of the Indira Gandhi Government on the grounds of 'internal Disturbance'.
 
• Till date, National Emergency has been declared three times in India in 1962, 1971 and 1975.
 
• The emergency of 1962 was declared on the grounds of external aggression on accounts of Chinese Aggression.
 
• In 1971, after attack by Pakistan emergency was declared.

 

 
 

 **Articles**
 **Emergency**
 
 

 Article 352
 
 
 
• **National Emergency.**
 
• Can be declared on the grounds of War, External aggression and Armed Rebellion.
 
 
 
 

 Article 356
 
 
 
• **President' s Rule or Constitutional Emergency.**
 
• Due to the failure of Constitutional machinery in any state.
 
 
 
 

 Article 360
 
 
 
• **Financial Emergency.**
 
• Declared when there is a threat of financial instability in the country.

questions.question: The Khurda Uprising took place in the year:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3**. Paika rebellion took place in **1817**.

 
• The rebellion was an outrage of the tribals against the extortionist land revenue policy of Britishers.
 
• **After the second Anglo-Maratha war, Odisha was captured** by the Britishers and the **King of Khurda was dethroned in 1803.**
 
• Land revenue was imposed on the Paiks (militia) who previously enjoyed tax-free land tenures for their military service to the king, high taxes were imposed on salts and were asked to pay taxes in silver coins instead of their cowrie currency.
 
• **In 1813, Bakshi Jagbandhu**, military chief of the king assisted by the Khonds, local zamindar **revolted against Britishers.**
 
• They were able to regain the area from the East India Company.
 
• But later Britishers regained the control and a few rebels surrendered till 1817.
 
• Other rebels continued Guerilla wars against the company and burnt their offices.
 
• **Finally, in 1825, Jagbandhu surrendered** after negotiations with Britishers and Paika were able to get remissions in tax.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of sound wave?
questions.solution:
**Option 2** is the correct answer. Nature is not a characteristic of the sound wave.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Sound: It is a form of energy produced by vibration or disturbance that propagates in a medium.

 
• It travels in the form of longitudinal waves (Compression or rarefaction)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8b82b5e660f7984a80ca8aa17e891e0e40ffd516b2e8892cb4b96bc17c35bc05.png] 

 
• The audible range for human ears is 20 Hertz to 20 Kilo Hertz.

 
 

 **Characteristic**
 **Explanation**
 
 

 Amplitude
 
 
 
• It refers to the extent to which the particles of a medium are displaced through which the sound wave passes.
 
• Amplitude determines the loudness of the soundwave.
 
 
 
 

 Wavelength
 
 
 
• The distance between two similar points in a wave is called its wavelength.
 
 
 
 

 Frequency
 
 
 
• The number of waves passing through a point in one second is called the frequency of a wave.
 
• The frequency determines pitch.

questions.question: In which of the following period Ostriches were found in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3**. The Ostriches were found in the Palaeolithic period in India.

 
 

 **Period**
 **Facts**
 
 

 Megalithic Period
 
 
 
• The megalithic period of India dates back to around** 1000 BC**.
 
• The sites seem to be concentrated more in south India.
 
• The major megalithic** structures are burial sites where huge stones have been erected.**
 
 
 
 

 Neolithic Period
 
 
 
• The **New Stone Age.**
 
• 7,000 BC - 2,500 BC.
 
• Polished stone tools made with harder rocks.
 
• Animal domestication started.
 
• People led a settled life and used to cultivate the land.
 
• The states of Karnataka, Meghalaya, Tamil Nadu, and Bihar have major sites of this period.
 
 
 
 

 Palaeolithic Period
 
 
 
• The **old Stone Age.**
 
• 500,000 BC-10,000 BC.
 
• Unpolished tools made up of quartz.
 
• No agriculture, pottery or knowledge of fire.
 
• In India, the sites have been found at Belan Valley, near Narmada and Tungabhadra rivers, in Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, and Chhota Nagpur Plateau.
 
 
 
 

 Mesolithic Period
 
 
 
• The** Middle Stone Age.**
 
• 10,000 BC - 7,000 BC.
 
• The climate became warmer and plain cultivation started during the last phase.
 
• 
 
Tools: Pointed microliths, scrapers, and blades.

 
 
• 
 
Belan valley and middle part of Narmada valley are the major sites in India.

questions.question: Who among the following suggested that life must have developed from simple inorganic molecule?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2.**

 
• **J.B.S. Haldane** opinioned that life must have developed from the simple inorganic molecule in the **Oparin-Haldane Hypothesis.**
 
• According to him the process of evolution from inorganic to organic would have taken in multiples events owing to change of conditions on earth.

 
 

 **Scientists**
 **Major Findings/ Researches**
 
 

 Stanley L. Miller
 
 
 
• Performed experiments and prepared amino acids (major constituents of proteins) from inorganic compounds by replicating the early earth conditions in the lab.
 
• This experiment is known as the **Miller-Urey experiment.**
 
 
 
 

 J.B.S. Haldane
 
 
 
• **Oparin-Haldane Hypothesis:** The life must have developed from the simple inorganic molecule.
 
• Developed Mathematical Theory of Population Genetics along with other two fellow scientists.
 
 
 
 

 Gregor Mendel
 
 
 
• Known as the **father of modern genetics.**
 
 
 
 

 Charles Darwin
 
 
 
• Authored '**On the Origin of Species'.**
 
• The theory of animal ancestry of human beings was inferred from this book.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a process of water cycle?
questions.solution:
**Option 2** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Ammonification is not a process of the water cycle.
 
• It is an important** process of the Nitrogen cycle.**
 
• **Decomposition of organic compounds containing Nitrogen to release Ammonia or Ammonium** compounds is called Ammonification.
 
• **Evaporation, Transpiration, Condensation and Precipitation** are the major process of the water cycle.

 
 

 **Process**
 **Explanation**
 
 

 Evaporation 
 
 
 
• The conversion of water in water vapours.
 
• In the water cycle water evaporates from the water bodies or soil.
 
 
 
 

 Transpiration
 
 
 
• The loss of water from the leaves of the plants** through stomata in leaves.**
 
 
 
 

 Condensation
 
 
 
• Conversion of **vapours into water.**
 
• The water evaporated from water bodies, plants and soil rises above in the atmosphere and cools down there due to low temperatures.
 
• This** leads to cloud formation**.
 
 
 
 

 Precipitation 
 
 
 
• The **water comes back down to earth in various forms like rain, snowfall, hails,** etc which is known as Precipitation.
 
 
 
 

*The **sun is the driving force** behind the water cycle.

questions.question: Which of the Article of Indian Constitution tells about the election of President?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3**. Article 54 discusses the election of the president.

 
• The President of India is elected by **members of an electoral college **instead of direct elections. Following are the members of an electoral college:

 
 
• Elected members of both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
 
• Elected members of state legislative assemblies.
 
• Elected members of legislative assemblies of UTs of Delhi and Puducherry.
 
 
 
• The method adopted for the election of the President is a** system of proportional representation by the means single transferable vote.**
 
• The** voter is required to indicate the preference on the ballot paper** and he can mark as many preferences as the number of candidates.
 
• The voting takes place in phases and the candidate securing the least number of first preferences is eliminated in each phase.
 
• The process is carried on and at last, a person securing the required quota of votes stands elected.

 

 
 

 **Article Number**
 **Subject Matter**
 
 

 Article 51A
 Fundamental Duties.
 
 

 Article 53
 Executive Power of Union (vested in The President).
 
 

 Article 54
 Election of the President.
 
 

 Article 51
 Promotion of International Peace and Harmony (DPSP).
